description: A two-PC local-network IoT OTA update and fleet management demo. PC-A runs FastAPI + React dashboard. PC-B runs React simulator with graphic ESP32 device cards (SVG LEDs, LCD, PCB board), template picker, presets, and C++ code viewer. Devices sync in real time via WebSocket.

userStories.title: Project Scaffold & Monorepo Setup
userStories.description: As a developer, I want a clean monorepo project structure so that PC-A (dashboard) and PC-B (simulator) can be run independently while sharing types.
acceptanceCriteria: Root folder C:\Users\mujaw\Downloads\IOT with subdirs: backend/, dashboard/, simulator/, shared/
backend/ is a FastAPI app that starts with: uvicorn main:app --reload --port 8000
dashboard/ is a React + Vite + TailwindCSS app configured on port 5173
simulator/ is a React + Vite + TailwindCSS app configured on port 3000
shared/types.ts exports TypeScript interfaces: Device, FirmwareVersion, OTAStatus, LogEntry, Group
Both frontends import shared types via relative path alias
Root README.md documents how to run all three services
backend/ has requirements.txt with: fastapi, uvicorn, python-multipart
Both frontend apps run npm run dev without errors
Backend starts without errors
userStories.notes: Scaffold complete. Both Vite apps start. Typecheck passes. Backend imports verified.

userStories.title: Backend — Device Registry & WebSocket Event Bus
userStories.description: As the system, I want a FastAPI backend that maintains in-memory device state and broadcasts real-time events via WebSocket so both UIs stay in sync instantly.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /api/devices/register accepts { id, mac, firmware, group, template } and stores device in memory
DELETE /api/devices/{id} removes device and broadcasts device_removed event
GET /api/devices returns all devices with full current state
POST /api/devices/{id}/status updates device gpio, uptime, ota_progress fields
POST /api/devices/{id}/logs appends a log entry { level, msg, timestamp }
GET /api/devices/{id}/logs returns last 100 log lines
WebSocket endpoint /ws/events broadcasts JSON events to all connected clients
Event types broadcast: device_registered, device_removed, device_status, device_log, ota_started, ota_progress, ota_complete
CORS middleware allows origins: http://localhost:5173, http://localhost:3000, and all LAN IPs (allow_origins=['*'] for demo)
All endpoints return proper HTTP status codes and JSON
Backend runs without errors after: uvicorn main:app --reload

userStories.title: Backend — Firmware Store & OTA Endpoints
userStories.description: As the system, I want the backend to manage firmware versions and serve OTA update endpoints so simulator devices can poll, download, and confirm updates.
acceptanceCriteria: firmware/ directory exists with placeholder files: v1.0.0.bin, v1.1.0.bin, v1.2.0.bin (can be empty/text files)
GET /api/firmware returns list of versions with: version, size, changelog, date fields
POST /api/ota/push accepts { device_ids: [], version } and marks those devices as ota_pending, broadcasts ota_started event
POST /api/ota/rollback accepts { device_id, version } and initiates rollback flow
GET /ota/update/{device_id} returns 200 + file content if device has pending update, 304 if up to date
POST /api/ota/reset accepts { device_id, version } to reset firmware to chosen version
POST /api/devices/{id}/status with { ota_progress: 100, state: 'complete' } clears ota_pending and broadcasts ota_complete
All OTA state changes broadcast appropriate WebSocket events
Backend runs without errors

userStories.title: Backend — Groups & Config Push Endpoints
userStories.description: As a user, I want group management and config push endpoints so devices can be organized and configured remotely from PC-A.
acceptanceCriteria: GET /api/groups returns list of groups with { name, device_count }
POST /api/groups accepts { name } and creates a new group
PUT /api/devices/{id}/group accepts { group } and updates device group
POST /api/config/push accepts { device_ids: [], config: {} } and broadcasts config_pushed WebSocket event to targeted devices
Config payload stored on device state as device.config field
Default groups pre-seeded on startup: floor-1, floor-2, rooftop
Backend runs without errors

userStories.title: Shared SVG Components — ESP32 Board, LED, LCD
userStories.description: As a developer, I want shared SVG React components for the ESP32 PCB board, LED indicator, and 16x2 LCD so both PC-A and PC-B render identical visuals.
acceptanceCriteria: shared/components/Esp32Board.tsx renders an SVG ESP32-WROOM board: blue PCB, gold pin pads on both sides, chip rectangle labeled ESP32, antenna line
Esp32Board accepts props: pins: { [pinName]: 'HIGH' | 'LOW' }, size?: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg'
shared/components/LedIndicator.tsx renders SVG circle: ON = amber/yellow with radial gradient + CSS pulse glow keyframe animation, OFF = dark grey #374151 no glow
LedIndicator accepts props: on: boolean, label: string
shared/components/LcdScreen.tsx renders 16x2 LCD: dark green background #0a2e0a, amber monospace text #fbbf24, border glow, exactly 16 char cells x 2 rows
LcdScreen accepts props: row1: string (max 16 chars), row2: string (max 16 chars), backlight?: boolean
Components importable from both dashboard/ and simulator/ via path alias
All three components render without errors in browser
Verify in browser: LED glows/pulses when on=true, dims when on=false; LCD shows two rows of text correctly

userStories.title: PC-B Simulator — WebSocket Hook & Device State Engine
userStories.description: As the simulator, I want a React hook that connects to the backend WebSocket and a simulation engine that runs per-device heartbeat loops so the dashboard stays alive without manual interaction.
acceptanceCriteria: useWebSocket.ts hook connects to ws://[API_BASE]/ws/events and exposes: lastEvent, connectionStatus
useDeviceSimulator.ts hook accepts a device object and runs setInterval every 2000ms
Every 2s: POST /api/devices/{id}/status with current uptime (incrementing), gpio state
Every 5s: POST /api/devices/{id}/logs with a realistic log line (rotates through: OTA check no update, LED1 ON D0 HIGH, heap free 218KB, WiFi RSSI -47, etc.)
For LED template: gpio reflects last applied preset (D0/D1 HIGH or LOW)
For LCD template: logs reflect last applied LCD text preset
Simulation loop starts on device registration, cleans up (clearInterval) on device deletion
VITE_API_BASE env var used for all HTTP and WebSocket URLs
No console errors when running

acceptanceCriteria: PC-B app renders at http://localhost:3000 with dark slate background #0f172a
Top header: app title 'ESP32 Device Simulator', dashboard connection status badge, device count
Device grid: 3 columns on wide screen, each card contains: Esp32Board SVG (sm size), device ID, template icon (💡 or 🖥), group badge, firmware version badge, online/offline status badge, uptime
NO pin states, no sensor readings shown on home card
Online card: normal color; Offline card: PCB SVG dims to greyscale, 'POWERED OFF' overlay text
During OTA: card shows animated flicker on PCB + progress bar (0-100%) + 'FLASHING...' label
Each card has [✕] delete button — calls DELETE /api/devices/{id} on confirm
Each card has [👁 Open Device] button — navigates to device detail route
Last slot in grid is always the [+ Add Device] card
Devices received via WebSocket device_registered/device_removed events update grid in real time
Verify in browser: grid renders, cards show correct template icons, delete works, grid updates on WebSocket events

userStories.title: PC-B Simulator — Add Device Modal
userStories.description: As a user, I want an Add Device modal with a template picker so I can spawn a new simulated ESP32 that auto-registers on PC-A.
acceptanceCriteria: Clicking [+ Add Device] card opens a modal overlay

One template must be selected before confirming (default: 2-LED Controller)
Confirm button: POST /api/devices/register with all fields including template

userStories.title: PC-B Simulator — C++ Code Viewer Modal & OTA Reset Modal
userStories.description: As a demo presenter, I want a syntax-highlighted C++ code viewer and a firmware reset modal so I can show real Arduino code and demonstrate rollback.

Reset/Rollback modal opens on [↺ Reset Firmware] click

Both modals accessible without errors
